Osaka Okonomiyaki

The Osaka savoury pancake — cabbage bound with a dashi batter, griddled thick, then covered in sweet-sharp sauce, mayonnaise and dancing bonito flakes. It translates roughly as "grilled how you like it", which is the whole point.

★★★★★★★★★★4.6(1,042)Rated 4.6 out of 5 from 1042 reviews 40 min total Serves 4 servings Medium Japanese
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

Grated nagaimo yam adds a mucilaginous starch that makes the interior fluffy and custardy rather than dense — it is the single ingredient that separates restaurant okonomiyaki from a heavy cabbage fritter. Cooking undisturbed for five minutes per side builds the crust that holds the loose batter together.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Whisk the flour, dashi, salt and grated yam into a smooth batter and rest it, covered, in the fridge for 30 minutes.

  2. Just before cooking, beat in the eggs, then fold through the cabbage, spring onions and pickled ginger. The mixture should look like barely-bound cabbage, not batter with cabbage in it.

  3. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Spoon in half the mixture and shape it into a 20 cm round about 3 cm thick. Do not press it down.

  4. Lay half the pork belly slices over the top in a single layer.

  5. Cook undisturbed for 5 to 6 minutes until the base is deeply golden and the edges look set.

  6. Flip confidently in one motion, using a plate if you are nervous. Cook the pork side for 5 minutes, then press down gently once.

  7. Flip back for a final minute to re-crisp, then slide onto a plate.

  8. Zigzag with okonomiyaki sauce and mayonnaise, scatter with aonori, and finish with a generous pile of bonito flakes — they will curl and wave in the rising steam.

Chef’s Tips

  • Shred the cabbage finely but not to a mush; 3 mm ribbons hold structure and stay sweet.
  • No okonomiyaki sauce? Mix 3 tbsp ketchup, 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tsp sugar.
  • Resist pressing the pancake while it cooks. Compressing it squeezes out the air you need for a fluffy centre.

Pairing Suggestions

  • Cold lager or a highball
  • Serve with miso soup and pickles
  • Finish with mochi ice cream

Storage & Reheating

Best fresh. Keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 minutes a side and re-sauce afterwards.
